OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `create_clone` (cards/base.py) IS a memberwise copy now. `ClonePreservingMutability` is `AbstractModel.MutableClone` (a MemberwiseClone) and only THEN `DeepCloneFields` (CardModel.cs:1193-1216) and `AfterCloned` (:1218-1239), so the sim opens with `clone.__dict__.update(card.__dict__)` and the two override passes only re-point what must not be shared (`combat`, and the enchantment/affliction that DeepCloneFields re-creates). Everything the guard named now rides along: the LIVE KEYWORD SET (`_keywords = GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local)`, :1196-1200 -- Music Box's Ethereal), the cloned `_energyCost` and its `_localModifiers` (:1202 -> CardEnergyCost.cs:411-421 -- SetThisCombat, AddThisTurn, free-this-turn), the cloned `_dynamicVars` (:1201 -- a grown Rampage clones grown) and `BaseReplayCount` (Hidden Gem). `CreateClone`'s own tail, `ExhaustOnNextPlay = false` (:2178), is the last line. ONE MORE FINDING, and it is the reason the fix could not be a one-liner: DeepCloneFields re-attaches with `EnchantInternal` (:1204-1209 -> :1491-1498), which checks NO CanEnchant and does NOT run `ModifyCard` -- EnchantmentModel.cs:350-353 says why in as many words, "It is NOT called when a card is cloned, because the enchantment's effects will already be reflected in the card's values." The sim only had the normal `attach`, and re-running it on a memberwise copy is not merely redundant, it THROWS for Souls, whose CanEnchant demands the Exhaust its own ModifyCard removes. `Enchantment.attach_internal` is that path. EXECUTED, old -> new: keyword False->True, free-this-turn cost 1->0, base_replay_count 0->3, a twice-played Rampage 9->19. Pinned by test/test_create_clone_memberwise.py. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27 (partly closed). CLOSED: the enchantment and affliction halves. `trash_heap_cards.py:_clone` (lines 20-25) is now a one-line delegate to `create_clone` (cards/base.py:57-83), which re-attaches a `clone_preserving_mutability()` copy of the source's enchantment and a copy of its affliction -- CardModel.DeepCloneFields' two blocks (CardModel.cs:1204-1215). The record's headline observable -- duplicate a Spiral-enchanted Attack and the copy is vanilla -- is gone, which is the whole point of this card. STILL OPEN: `create_clone` rebuilds from the class (`type(card)()` + replayed upgrades) where C#'s CreateClone is a MEMBERWISE copy plus DeepCloneFields (CardModel.cs:2168-2181 -> AbstractModel.MutableClone:162-169), so the copy still loses the cloned `_energyCost` object (CardModel.cs:1202 -- SetThisCombat / AddThisTurn / free-this-turn overrides), `BaseReplayCount`, and the live keyword set (CardModel.cs:1195-1200). EXECUTED: a Spiral-enchanted card with `base_replay_count = 3` and `set_cost_this_combat(0)` clones with enchantment `spiral` but `base_replay_count` 3 -> 0 and cost 0 -> 1. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/anger's OnPlay entry (rule 3). The BLAST-RADIUS clause below about CardSelectCmd's MinSelect auto-select is unaffected and untouched. HISTORY -- WHAT THE DIVERGENCE WAS: The selection filter and the loop are faithful: C#'s `filter: c => c.Type == Attack || c.Type == Power` with MinSelect 1 (DualWield.cs:26-30) == `predicate=lambda c: c.card_type in (CardType.ATTACK, CardType.POWER)`, the null/empty result skips everything on both sides, and the copies go to PileType.Hand. THE COPY IS NOT A CLONE: `_clone` (trash_heap_cards.py:18-24) is `type(card)()` plus replayed upgrades. The sim's clone helper builds a FRESH instance and replays `upgrade()` `upgrade_level` times instead of reproducing `CardModel.CreateClone()` (CardModel.cs:2168-2181 -> RunState.CloneCard:394-399 -> AbstractModel.MutableClone:162-169 + CardModel.DeepCloneFields:1193-1216), which carries over the live keyword set, the cloned `_energyCost` object (so SetThisCombat / AddThisTurn / free-this-turn overrides survive), `BaseReplayCount`, and DEEP-CLONES the card's Enchantment (1204-1209) and Affliction (1210-1214) onto the copy. The sim's copy loses all of that. Observable: duplicate a Spiral-enchanted Attack -- in the game the copy is also Spiral-enchanted and replays when played; in the sim it is vanilla. LIVE: enchantments.py:372-375 (Spiral) accepts any ATTACK card and events/spiraling_whirlpool.py:46 attaches it to a player-chosen deck card; events/self_help_book.py:71 and events/grave_of_the_forgotten.py:47 are two more ported attach sites. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/anger's OnPlay entry (rule 3). Dual Wield is the card that makes this most visible, because copying an ENCHANTED Attack is the whole point of the card.
